### Events

[Spotlight Sundays: Japanese American Legacies of Resistance November 15 from 1:00 pm – 2:30 pm This Sunday, we are stepping into the historical legacy that inspired OMCA’s latest special exhibition, BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration. With opening remarks by OMCA Executive Director Lori Fogarty, we will engage with this present moment in American history with the clarity and learnings of the past. Learn More](https://museumca.org/event/spotlight-sundays-japanese-american-legacies-of-resistance/)

[Holiday Market at the Museum! December 5 from 11:30 am – 4:00 pm Celebrating the winter season, OMCA partners with local vendors to offer an unusual and tempting array of items great for gift giving—from jewelry and art prints to beautiful textiles, gifts for your four-legged friends, and plenty of other unique finds. Learn More](https://museumca.org/event/holiday-market-at-the-museum/)

[Special Guest Gallery Chat: Questions 27 & 28 with Author Karen Tei Yamashita December 5 from 12:00 pm – 1:00 pm Join acclaimed author Karen Tei Yamashita for a Special Guest Gallery Chat in conjunction with OMCA’s current exhibition, Be Here / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration. Born in Oakland in 1951, Yamashita is a member of the Sansei generation, the grandchildren of Japanese immigrants. With both of her parents incarcerated at Topaz, Utah, during World War II, Yamashita brings a personal connection to this history. Learn More](https://museumca.org/event/special-guest-gallery-chat-questions-27-28-with-author-karen-tei-yamashita/)

[Special Guest Gallery Chat: Remembering Together with Judy Sakaki and Lana Masako Wong December 5 from 1:00 pm – 2:00 pm Join Judy Sakaki and her granddaughter, Lana Masako Wong, for a special intergenerational Gallery Chat in conjunction with our current exhibition, Be Here / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration. Through conversation and personal stories, they will explore how the legacy of Japanese American incarceration is remembered and passed down across generations. Learn More](https://museumca.org/event/special-guest-gallery-chat-remembering-together-with-judy-sakaki-and-lana-masako-wong/)

## Spotlight on OMCA

![](https://museumca.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Lori-Fogarty-High-Resv-118-6x9-1-1024x751-1.webp)

2024 CAMMY AWARD WINNER LORI FOGARTY

The annual CAMMY Award recognizes extraordinary museum supporters, professionals, and institutions that have made outstanding contributions to California museums. OMCA is elated to announce that this year, CAM has recognized one of our very own, Executive Director and CEO, Lori Fogarty! This award highlights her dedicated leadership throughout her extensive career, including within her role of nearly two decades at OMCA, an institution that centers community engagement, field innovation, and a commitment to inclusivity and diversity. Congratulations, Lori!

![](https://museumca.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/2022IMLSMedals_JULY20_0363-1-1024x488-1.webp)

WINNER OF THE 2022 NATIONAL MEDAL FOR MUSEUM AND LIBRARY SERVICE

The Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS) awarded OMCA one of only six recipients of the 2022 National Medal for Museum and Library Service, the nation’s highest honor for museums and libraries making significant and exceptional contributions to their communities.
